diagnosis: The failure is primarily an instruction-model gap. The compiler preserves the abstract mass rule in structured JSON but drops it from generator_instruction, while the content model has no member plan that resolves a COMPOUND_SET into two or three complete objects. The singular morphology language then wins and produces one loop with one cabin. Explicit member resolution changes the assembly outcome without changing the visual system.
not_supported_by_this_test: Restricting future-object morphology to fixed archetypes
Hard-coding toroidal, crescent, or oval members into the global grammar
Treating the shared apricot color leak as an assembly failure
recommended_next_change: Add a generic assembly member plan to the generation-content/brief path for multi-object modes, and serialize subject_assembly_count plus subject_mass_rule into generator_instruction. Validate that COMPOUND_SET names 2–3 complete member roles and rejects over-fusion, without hard-coding the test objects.
